_comment: Eval ground truth for the FINAL system (retrieval on, get_file_context tool available). Read only by evals/ — agent nodes must never see this file. QA-105 is expected to score needs_info until the bounded-tool commit lands; that red-to-green flip is deliberate.

QA-101.rationale: Clean implementation: limit/offset with correct defaults, total_count over all non-archived orders, tests cover default and offset pages.

QA-102.rationale: EMAIL_PATTERN only matches lowercase and is compiled without re.IGNORECASE, so USER@EXAMPLE.COM is rejected — AC-2 fails. The added tests only exercise lowercase addresses, so they pass while missing the defect.

QA-103.rationale: Discount logic and threshold are correct, but int(base * 100) / 100 truncates instead of rounding half-even — a defect under the runbook money rule even though the test (89.95) passes. Without the retrieved runbook this diff looks like a pass: this is the RAG-ablation fixture.

QA-104.rationale: The diff hardcodes RETENTION_DAYS = 90, but no source (ticket, diff, glossary, runbook) defines the retention cutoff — the glossary explicitly says ops owns it. AC-1 is unverifiable; AC-2 is verified via the existing archived-status filter in list_orders.

QA-105.rationale: The diff only shows notify_order_created(order) being called; verifying AC-2 requires reading app/notifications.py (not in the diff), which confirms the body includes order id and total. Single-call review without the tool should honestly return unclear on AC-2.

QA-106.rationale: Summary fields are separate, tax is 8% of subtotal only (shipping untaxed), rounding uses round() (half-even — runbook compliant), and tests cover both an itemized and an empty order.

QA-107.rationale: gift_wrap is added correctly, but the diff also deletes the validate_quantity call from create_order — a regression of existing validation behavior that AC-2 explicitly protects. The runbook holds diffs responsible for what they remove.

QA-108.rationale: Items are attached at construction, the response total flows through order_total over real items, and a regression test asserts the itemized total. Ticket body contains fictional PII (email, phone, card number) to exercise redaction.

QA-109.rationale: AC says 10 or more items (>= 10); the diff uses item_count > 10, so an exactly-10-item order still pays shipping. The added test at 12 items passes and misses the boundary — which testing-conventions.md calls out as insufficient.

QA-110.rationale: Noisy-looking refactor, but behavior is correct: promo applies to subtotal before shipping, the threshold evaluates the discounted amount (test at 110.00 - 20% = 88.00 proves it), and no-promo totals are unchanged.
